Emma — thanks for the clear note and for attaching the PO. Looping in Marcus (finance) and Laura (sales ops) so we can scope the operational side.

High level: we can support either approach, but each has tradeoffs for VAT handling and AP automation. Two options we typically recommend:

1) Single consolidated invoice with a per-line entity allocation table
   - One invoice ID, line items split with an "Entity" column and VAT number per line.
   - Single remit-to section with explicit routing table that directs payments to multiple bank accounts (we can include per-line IBAN/ACH info).
   - Pros: single invoice for your systems; easier order-of-operations.
   - Cons: some AP systems prefer distinct invoices per legal entity for automatic posting.

2) Separate invoices per legal entity
   - Three invoices, each shows only the lines charged to that legal entity and its VAT number.
   - Pros: simplest for GL posting and local VAT returns.
   - Cons: requires Redwood to generate multiple invoices and more billing transactions.

A few clarifying Qs that will determine the recommended path:
- Do your ERPs require distinct invoice numbers to auto-post by legal entity?
- Do you need net-of-VAT amounts per entity or gross?
- Any currency conversion or inter-entity netting planned?

I attached a short spreadsheet with sample layouts for both options (redwood_split_options.xlsx). Once we have your preference on invoice numbering and VAT presentation, Marcus can prepare the exact template and GL mapping.

Proposed next step: if it's helpful, we can schedule a 20-minute call with AP and Marcus to confirm remit-to fields and PO mapping.

Thanks, Soojin — that framing helps. Answers below:

- Our ERP (NetBooks) requires unique invoice numbers per legal entity to fully automate posting. If a single invoice is used, we would need a CSV mapping with invoice number + GL account + entity in order to auto-split, which is an extra step for AP.
- We need VAT shown per entity (gross and VAT amount); net-of-VAT per entity is preferred for our tax team.
- Currency: all lines will be USD. No inter-entity netting planned; each entity will remit its portion to the bank account indicated.

Attached is our entity mapping CSV with legal names, VAT numbers, and preferred remit-to instructions. For speed, our preference would be to receive three invoice numbers (one per entity) unless Redwood prefers to keep a single invoice number and supply the CSV mapping at the time of invoicing.

Attachments: entity_mapping.csv

Subject: Internal: Recommended billing workflow for NovoHealth split remittance

Team — I reviewed NovoHealth's mapping and PO. My recommendation to minimize manual work on both sides:

Step A — Invoice model
- Create one consolidated invoice (single external document) for customer visibility, but issue three internal invoice numbers (linked to the consolidated PDF) so our AR system can record revenue to the correct legal entities. The consolidated PDF will show a table mapping internal invoice numbers to legal entities and VAT amounts.

Step B — Remit & bank routing
- Include a remit-routing appendix with per-entity bank details. We will accept separate payments to up to 3 different bank accounts. We need NovoHealth AP to confirm the exact remittance reference string they will send so payments reconcile automatically.

Step C — Accounting postings
- GL codes must be supplied by NovoHealth per entity (we will map these to Redwood's cost centers). Laura, can you capture the GL mapping and confirm whether we should create subsidiary invoice records in Zuora/Chargebee?

Step D — VAT documentation
- Each entity line will include VAT registration number and VAT amount. For EU/UK VAT we will need local tax codes — ask NovoHealth to confirm jurisdiction per entity if outside the US.

Risks/notes:
- If NetBooks refuses to auto-split by single invoice, fallback is to issue three separate invoices. That will incur incremental transaction overhead but is acceptable.

I'll draft the invoice template and the reconciliation CSV column spec. Attaching a short doc with bank formatting and expected remit string (acct_payment_instructions.docx).

-Marcus

Emma — thank you and team for the quick turnaround. Confirming the agreed plan below so we have it in writing: 

1) Invoice format
- Redwood will produce one consolidated PDF invoice for NovoHealth for PO 7890 for external reporting.
- Internally, Redwood will generate three internal invoice numbers (one per legal entity). The consolidated PDF will include a clear allocation table: internal_invoice_id | legal_entity_name | VAT_number | line_total_ex_VAT | VAT_amount | remit_to_account.

2) Remittance
- NovoHealth AP will remit three separate payments (one per legal entity) to the bank accounts listed in the remit-routing appendix. Each payment should include the internal invoice id as the payment reference to ensure automatic reconciliation.

3) VAT and reporting
- VAT will be shown per entity on the consolidated PDF. Marcus will ensure tax codes are present if any entity is in EU/UK jurisdiction.

4) Timeline and next steps
- Marcus will share the finalized invoicing template and reconciliation CSV spec by 2026-11-26.
